findings.body: Removing `escapeHtml` and passing `body` straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` turns every comment into executable HTML. A body such as `` or `` runs in other users' browsers. This also does not implement markdown: `**bold**` stays literal text while real tags execute. Keep HTML-escaping, or parse markdown through a sanitizing renderer and never feed raw user HTML to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

summary: Looks good is the wrong read — this is a stored XSS regression and should not merge. `Comment` previously HTML-escaped `body` before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. This PR deletes `escapeHtml` and injects `body` as raw HTML. There is no markdown parser and no sanitizer anywhere in the tree; a comment containing `` or an `javascript:` link runs in every reader's browser. The new comment claims bold/links, but `**bold**` still renders as literal text while real HTML executes. Restore escaping, or parse markdown into React nodes / sanitized HTML (e.g. a sanitizing markdown renderer). Do not pass unsanitized user content to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. **Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and feeds the raw comment body into dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so attacker-controlled HTML/JS executes in other users' browsers. Base still escaped the body; this is a clear critical XSS regression.
